# Results (draft)

*Numbers are generated by `scripts/make_figures.py` from the run outputs (tables: `outputs/paper/tables.md`;
figures: `outputs/paper/figures/`). Figures whose name ends in `_DATA` contain dataset images (CC BY-NC-SA) and are
kept out of git. All test sets were touched only after model selection; checkpoints are selected on synthetic
validation (zero-shot) or on the real validation split (few-shot settings).*

## 1. Zero-shot transfer: synthetic-only training segments real panoramics

A U-Net trained only on simulated panoramics rendered from 374 ToothFairy3 CBCT volumes, with the full domain
randomization (DR), segments the teeth on 187 real DENTEX test panoramics with Dice 0.774 [95% CI 0.765, 0.783]
(Table E). It also **enumerates** them: per-tooth FDI Dice is 0.604 [0.582, 0.626], 91.2% of annotated teeth are
detected, and 89.9% [88.0, 91.8] of detected teeth receive the correct FDI number. The model never saw a real image or
a real label.

DENTEX tooth polygons are coarse: straight edges, and they include the gaps between teeth. Our predictions follow the
tooth contours (Fig. `fig_dentex_overlays_DATA`), so Dice understates boundary quality. We therefore also report the
boundary-insensitive tooth-level measures above. On held-out synthetic test volumes (105 CBCTs), the same model
reaches teeth 0.882, inferior alveolar canal 0.745 / 0.763 (left / right), sinus 0.709, pulp 0.668 and incisive
canal 0.460. The predicted canals are anatomically plausible on real images (below the molar roots, rising into the
ramus), but DENTEX has no canal labels; real canal accuracy is measured on CONTACT (Section 5).

## 2. Few-shot: CBCT pretraining replaces almost all real labels

Fine-tuning the zero-shot model on k labelled DENTEX images (sim→real) is compared with the same network trained
from ImageNet on the same k images (real-only). Both arms use the same schedule, and selection uses the real
validation split. Results are means over 3 seeds (Table A, Fig. `fig_fewshot_dentex`).

* With **4 labelled images**, sim→real reaches FDI Dice 0.702 ± 0.006 and numbering accuracy 0.933 ± 0.006. Real-only
  with **all 384** images reaches 0.647 ± 0.109 and 0.801 ± 0.183. Four labels plus simulation beat 96× more real labels
  on tooth identity.
* Sim→real is better on every metric at every label budget and far more stable across seeds (sd ≤ 0.013 on every
  metric, vs up to 0.21 for real-only numbering accuracy). Real-only per-tooth results depend strongly on which images
  are drawn.
* On teeth-union Dice the gap is smaller (0.894 vs 0.874 at 100%). The overall tooth outline in DENTEX's annotation
  style is learned from a handful of real images; identity and enumeration are not.

## 3. Which randomization factors matter (paired ablation)

Each factor was switched off in turn. The renders are paired with the reference (identical random draws except the
disabled factor), and every run uses a shorter schedule and 3 seeds (Table B, Fig. `fig_ablation`). The reference
reaches teeth Dice 0.734 ± 0.004 and numbering 0.911 ± 0.004.

* **Image-level noise is essential**: without it, teeth Dice drops by 0.436 [−0.547, −0.344] while synthetic test
  accuracy is unchanged or higher. The model fits the simulator but does not transfer.
* **Vendor-style processing** (background subtraction, unsharp masking, gamma) is the second most important factor
  (−0.066 [−0.095, −0.023]).
* The **geometric panoramic factors** (trough width, ghosts, blur outside the trough, arch jitter, spine) change teeth
  Dice by at most ±0.03. But removing any of them lowers numbering accuracy (−0.008 to −0.022; negative in all three
  seeds for trough width, ghosts, blur outside the trough, arch jitter and spine). They help the model tell the teeth apart rather
  than outline them.
* **Metal randomization, as configured, hurts**: removing it raises teeth Dice by +0.033 [+0.022, +0.047] in every seed
  (numbering −0.015). A narrower metal range recovers most but not all of this gain (Section 6).

## 4. Physics-based randomization vs. image translation (CycleGAN)

A standard CycleGAN was trained on synthetic renders and 2,098 unlabelled DENTEX images (NeBLa-style), and the
segmentation network on the translated renders with their original masks (Table C, Fig. `fig_cyclegan`). The
translated images look realistic (Fig. `fig_cyclegan_samples_DATA`), but the segmentation transfers far worse than
physics-based DR: teeth Dice 0.562 vs 0.774, and numbering accuracy 0.104 vs 0.899. Combining both is worse still
(0.509 / 0.216). The samples show why: unpaired translation **alters anatomy** (restorations vanish, tooth outlines and
gaps shift), so the projected labels no longer match the image. A simulator whose labels stay exact under every
randomization avoids this failure mode. *Caveat: single run of the standard architecture, without
structure-preserving losses.*

## 5. Third molar, canal and contact on real crops (CONTACT)

CONTACT provides 444 test crops (227 × 227) around the lower third molar, with molar and canal masks and a CBCT-derived
contact label. We trained a crop model on matching synthetic crops (~23 mm field of view; the scale was estimated by
matching third-molar size), initialised from the panoramic model (Table D, Figs. `fig_fewshot_contact`,
`fig_contact_overlays_DATA`).

* **Zero-shot segmentation:** molar Dice 0.611 and canal Dice 0.436–0.478. Molar outlines are often tight (0.85–0.95).
  Errors are mostly the neighbouring second molar being segmented, and CONTACT's canal masks are drawn as wider bands
  than our projected canal lumen.
* **2D overlap cannot detect contact:** the predicted molar–canal overlap gives AUC 0.510, and 0.468 for contact vs.
  overlap-without-contact (group 1 vs 3), i.e. chance. This is the radiological problem the dataset was built around.
* **Contact head trained on CBCT-derived labels:** for each third molar we computed the 3D tooth–canal distance from the
  CBCT labels (contact := the labels touch, ≤ 0.52 mm; 33% of 583 molars) and trained a classification head on
  synthetic crops only. On the real test set it reaches AUC 0.596 [0.538, 0.656], and 0.575 for group 1 vs 3. A weak
  but real signal that 2D overlap does not provide. For reference, CONTACT's expert-scored radiographic signs give AUC
  0.54 summed and 0.72 for the best single sign (canal discontinuity). Looser contact definitions transfer worse
  (≤ 1 mm: 0.564; ≤ 2 mm: 0.515; validation agrees), so the a-priori definition is kept.
* **Few-shot contact:** CBCT pretraining helps when real labels are scarce. With 9 labelled crops: contact AUC
  0.582 ± 0.010 vs 0.450 ± 0.028, and canal Dice 0.610 vs 0.356. With 44: 0.601 vs 0.532. From 88 crops the two arms are
  equal. From 220 crops real-only training is better (0.676–0.710 vs 0.627–0.672): the synthetic contact prior does not
  carry over to CONTACT's harder official test split once enough real labels exist. The validation AUC of sim→real
  models (0.81–0.86) is far above their test AUC. CONTACT's official test is harder than its train/validation pool
  (ground-truth-overlap AUC 0.717 vs 0.763), and its crops are somewhat blurrier.

## 6. Follow-up: retuning the randomization ranges

The ablation suggested two changes, tested under the same paired protocol and schedule (3 seeds; Table F,
Fig. `fig_dr_followup`):

* **Narrower metal range** (×0.8–1.5 instead of ×1–3): teeth Dice +0.024 [+0.014, +0.031] and numbering −0.009. This is
  better than the reference in every seed, but slightly below switching metal off entirely (+0.033). The original range
  over-brightens restorations; most of the harm comes from its upper end.
* **Wider image-level ranges** (photon count, read noise, detector blur, background subtraction, unsharp masking, gamma):
  teeth Dice +0.031 [+0.020, +0.042] and per-tooth FDI Dice +0.033 (positive in every seed), with numbering unchanged
  (+0.003). This is the only change that improves outline and per-tooth Dice without costing enumeration.
* **Both together** (metal off + wider image ranges): the highest teeth Dice, 0.779 (+0.044 [+0.036, +0.058]). But
  numbering falls by 0.017, negative in all three seeds.

So the image-level factors were under-randomized, and widening them is a free gain. Metal is a trade-off: less or no
metal randomization improves the tooth outline, but lowers numbering slightly. On synthetic test volumes, implant Dice is
lower in all four variants (0.54–0.61 vs 0.66). With no real implant labels and few implants in the synthetic test
set, we keep metal randomization at the narrower range rather than removing it. *These are short-schedule runs; the
headline zero-shot model (Section 1) uses the original ranges.*

## Limitations to state

* Real-image evaluation covers teeth (DENTEX) and third molar / canal / contact (CONTACT) only. Sinus, pulp and incisive
  canals are evaluated on synthetic data only; no public expert panoramic labels exist for them.
* DENTEX polygons are coarse; Dice rewards learning that annotation style, which favours models trained on DENTEX labels.
* CONTACT is distributed as crops, without patient IDs, so the validation split cannot be patient-disjoint from training.
* Single-run CycleGAN; 3 seeds elsewhere.
